misconceptions.description: Accepting an AI-suggested resume bullet that overstates a role or result the student cannot back up
misconceptions.trigger: AI rewrites 'helped with a club budget' into 'led financial operations'; learner keeps it
misconceptions.feedback: Keep the claim truthful. A resume line must match what you actually did and what you can defend in an interview. Reject the inflated verb and use one you can prove.

misconceptions.description: Believing that disclosing AI use means the work is dishonest or disallowed
misconceptions.trigger: learner hides that AI helped reword a bullet, fearing it looks like cheating
misconceptions.feedback: Disclosure documents the boundary, it does not confess wrongdoing. Note what the AI proposed, what you accepted, and what you rejected. Bounded, judged AI use is allowed and credible.

misconceptions.description: Adding job-posting keywords to the resume that do not reflect real experience just to pass a screener
misconceptions.trigger: learner pastes the posting's skill list into the resume verbatim without evidence
misconceptions.feedback: Match the role with true evidence, not copied keywords. If the posting wants 'data visualization', cite the chart you actually built, not the phrase alone.
